assessment:
One wish. Four cards in the 99 carry a library search, enumerated over all 96 entries by oracle text. Bloodstained Mire and Marsh Flats fetch a land, which is mana-analysis's business. Path to Exile hands the search to the creature's controller. Vampiric Tutor is the wish: {B}, instant, any card, on top of your library, two life and your next draw. deck-audit's tutors axis reads 1 copy.

The top-of-library clause sets the timing. Cast it at the last window before a draw you control: an opponent's end step before your untap, or your own upkeep. Then the card you bought is the card you draw. With Herald's Horn naming Vampire, cast it in your upkeep with the Horn's trigger on the stack: the Tutor resolves first, the Horn's look puts a Vampire creature card into your hand, and your draw step is still yours. Three of the four fetches below are Vampire creatures.

Where it points. The deck's own components are deep and the wish is not for them: a castable Vampire is drawn in 95.0% of games at mean turn 2.219, a draw engine in 83.5%, a lord or counter payoff in 80.0%, a free sacrifice outlet in 72.3%, a token multiplier in 67.9% (goldfish, seed 42, 10,000 games, model 5496ad1975b1, decklist 7be137d0). Three things are thin, and the assisted figure beside each is this one card and nothing else: a death drain, 37.2% unassisted against 48.2% assisted; Bloodthirsty Conqueror with a lifegain-loss half, 7.8% against 15.1%; Bloodletter of Aclazotz with Sanctum Seeker, 4.1% against 9.4%. engine.json draws the same gap as its fuel-to-wincon arrow and marks it a reading: the routes it points at have passing stacks (003, 004, 006); the act of tutoring into them does not.

Two things v1.1.1 did not change. Both verified kill routes still rest on one card each, and deck-audit prices Conqueror and Bloodletter as the deck's two single points of failure. The deck still holds one tutor. Elenda, the Dusk Rose and Blade of the Bloodchief came in as death payoffs; neither is in a passing stack, nothing measures either, and neither is a wish here.

One decision the numbers do not make. The pilot's direction says the lifegain infinite is out and drain is a theme; the 99 still holds Conqueror with Vito and with Sanguine Bond, both checker-passed. Log 004 lost to a tutored two-card infinite and the pilot wants a pod norm against them. Pointing this deck's only search at Conqueror is that move from the other chair. The Conqueror wish below is written for the board where the loop is the correct play. Whether it is the permitted play is a table call.

tutors.notes: {B}, instant, any card, on top, two life and your next draw. It reveals nothing, and there is no counterspell in the 99 to fight over it, so the only protection the wish has is that nobody sees it. Four rules. (1) Cast it at the end step before your untap or in your own upkeep, never earlier: a card on top for a turn is a card in removal range with a turn's warning. (2) Cast it only when you will cast the fetched card the turn it arrives. (3) Never buy a component the deck already finds; the rates above 67% are not what this card is for. (4) Read the black mana before the wish: 32 black sources against a 36 target (deck-audit colour-sources, Karsten 90%), black on curve 0.855 with rocks and 0.785 on lands alone (mana_analysis), and the two casts most worth buying are {1}{B}{B}{B} and {3}{B}{B}. Master of Dark Rites pays either: tap and sacrifice another creature for {B}{B}{B}, spendable on Vampire, Cleric and Demon spells. Bloodletter is a Vampire Demon, Conqueror a Vampire Knight, Celebrant a Vampire, and the token the Rites eats is a death, so Cordial Vampire, Elenda and the Blade are paid on the way. Pay the Tutor's two life without thinking about it early; stop paying life the turn a pinger or a drain seat is in range (log 005). When the read on an opponent is a wipe rather than a race, the behind fetch is Teferi's Protection instead of Despark: it is the only card in the 99 that phases out your permanents and stops your life total changing (enumerated over all 96 entries), and of the five protection cards it and Boros Charm are the two that reach Anointed Procession, Sanguine Bond and Elspeth; Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name creatures only.

targets.scenario: The end step of the opponent to your right, turn four. Viscera Seer, Cordial Vampire and three eminence tokens are on your battlefield. No card that drains on a death is on the board or in your hand. Every opponent is above 30. The Dimir seat has held four mana open for two turns and cast nothing. You have one black source untapped now and {W}{B} free on your turn.
targets.why:
You have the outlet and no bill. The deck holds exactly two cards that turn a death into life loss, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, and they are the whole of the goldfish's death-drain component: one of them is drawn in 37.2% of games, 25.2% by turn six, mean turn 4.305; with the wish, 48.2% and 34.3%. That is the thinnest component in the deck apart from the two one-card kill routes, and unlike the components above 67% it is one this card can replace.

Celebrant over Blood Artist, and the reason is oracle text: Blood Artist drains one target player per death, Celebrant each opponent. Three to one in a pod. Celebrant also gains you one per death, and with Vito or Sanguine Bond out that gain is a second point of loss on a seat you choose.

Say the read. Four open mana in a seat that has cast nothing for two turns is a sweeper in this model, not a fact on the board. If it is a sweeper, Celebrant makes it pay: every creature you lose drains each opponent for one, and Edgar rebuilds from the command zone. If it is a counterspell, the wish was cast at an end step and revealed nothing.

The limit. engine.json's conversion-to-output arrow (an outlet, Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant) carries no verified_by, no artifact measures an outlet and a payoff together, and the goldfish does not model a death drain at all. The rates above are for cards being drawn. Needs a stack scenario.

buy resilience instead of restraint where you can

targets.scenario: The end step of the opponent to your right, turn seven. Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose has been on your battlefield since turn four and has not been answered. Cruel Celebrant and Viscera Seer are beside him with two eminence tokens. Opponents are at 30, 26 and 9. You have seven lands, one black source untapped now and {3}{B}{B} free on your turn. No seat has left mana open at your end step since turn four.
targets.why:
This is the fetch that ends the game, and it is checker-passed twice. Stack 004 resolves Conqueror beside Vito as a deterministic, shortcut-legal table kill at zero additional mana from a 3-life seed, and the loop crosses an opponent's death mid-iteration. Stack 006 proves the same loop with Sanguine Bond in Vito's place. Both share one body, which is why Conqueror is the half to fetch: Vito and Sanguine Bond are interchangeable and Conqueror is not. On this board the seed is already there. Sacrifice a token to Viscera Seer: Celebrant gains you 1, Vito drains 1, Conqueror gains 1, and the triggers are mandatory. engine.json files that as a candidate line; whether you can decline it once all three are out needs a stack scenario.

Rates: 7.8% of games unassisted, 15.1% with the wish; 3.4% by turn six against 6.9%; mean turn 6.385. Carry the ticket; do not steer the whole game toward it.

Three prices. He lands the turn AFTER the search, so this is a two-turn commitment announced by a card you did not reveal. He is a 5/5 creature, so every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed creature removal; stack 004 names that cost in its own resolution. And {3}{B}{B} on seven lands leaves two, in a deck that has interaction castable at turn six in 26.9% of games.

The assumption: three end steps with no mana open is read as a table with no instant-speed answer up. That is a model of the table, not a fact about it. The table call in the assessment applies here more than anywhere.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: The end step of the opponent to your right, turn six. Sanctum Seeker, Edgar Markov and five other Vampires are on your battlefield, seven attackers on your turn. The seat across from you is at 14, the other two at 21 and 24. Master of Dark Rites is untapped with a token to feed it. You have six lands, one black source untapped now, and {1}{B}{B}{B} on your turn without the Rites.
targets.why:
Stack 003 is checker-passed on exactly this arithmetic. Seven attacking Vampires give seven Sanctum Seeker triggers; on your turn Bloodletter doubles each opponent's loss per trigger, so each seat loses 14, and the seat at 14 is eliminated by state-based actions before blockers are declared. Your own gain is not doubled; Bloodletter replaces only opponents' loss. Stack 003's board seeds the opponents at 21 and 14 and leaves the 21 seat at 7 with combat still to fight.

Count the attackers, then count again without Bloodletter. He has flying and no haste, so he does not attack the turn he lands; the seven in this scenario are seven other Vampires. Six attackers is 12 per seat, and a seat at 14 lives on 2. With six, wait a turn or fetch something else.

Read the mana. {1}{B}{B}{B} is the only cost in the 99 with three identical coloured pips (engine.json, enumerated over every mana cost in cards.json), and black is the deck's shortest colour at 32 sources against a 36 target. Master of Dark Rites changes it: tap and sacrifice another creature for {B}{B}{B}, spendable on Vampire, Cleric and Demon spells, and Bloodletter qualifies twice. The token it eats is a death for Cordial Vampire, Elenda and the Blade. engine.json's mana-to-wincon arrow through the Rites carries no verified_by.

Rates: 4.1% unassisted, 9.4% with the wish; 1.6% by turn six against 4.0%; mean turn 6.707, later than the Conqueror route, not faster. No artifact measures kill speed for either route.

citations.quote: each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale

targets.scenario: Your upkeep, turn six. The mono-red seat has had Purphoros, God of the Forge on the battlefield since turn three, and it is not a creature. You are at 17 from 40: Night's Whisper, Champion of Dusk, and eight entries' worth of pings. Elspeth, Storm Slayer is at four loyalty with two Soldier tokens beside her. Your hand holds no removal. You have {W}{B} plus one black source untapped, and Herald's Horn is not out.
targets.why:
Fetch the answer, not the threat. Purphoros, God of the Forge is {3}{R}, mana value 4, indestructible, and not a creature while its controller's devotion to red is under five. Of the eleven interactive copies deck-audit counts, two exile a noncreature indestructible permanent: Despark (exile target permanent with mana value 4 or greater) and Anguished Unmaking (exile target nonland permanent, you lose 3 life). Stroke of Midnight destroys, and an indestructible permanent cannot be destroyed. Path to Exile, Winds of Abandon, Elspeth's -3 and Vish Kal need a creature. Despark over Anguished Unmaking on this board because it costs {W}{B} and no life, and 3 life at 17 against a pinger is a real price. Anguished Unmaking is the fetch when the piece is under mana value 4.

Upkeep, not end step: this is the last window in which the wish is this turn's draw. Cast it, draw Despark, cast Despark in your first main phase before any Vampire enters and pings you. Every Vampire you cast is two entries, the body and the eminence token, and more under a doubler.

Why now rather than racing. Log 005 is this board: Elspeth exposed, tempo pushed, Purphoros pings finished the job before lethal landed. strategic_frame.json reports Forge on v1.1.0 against the playgroup pod with a Purphoros seat at 4 of 38 decided games for this deck; no Forge record exists on this sha. An enchantment that pings on every entry has the fastest clock at the table against a deck that pays life for cards.

The noncreature-answer component is drawn in 49.3% of games, 34.8% by turn six; 58.5% and 42.8% with the wish. That figure counts Stroke of Midnight, which does not answer this target. No stack verifies this line; it rests on oracle text and one rule.

switching from spending to defending one turn before it matters, not one after
the last profitable moment is now

gaps: All eleven stacks under stacks/ carry checker.verdict pass; five resolve boards that sit entirely inside the current 99 (002, 003, 004, 006, 010) and this guide cites 003, 004 and 006. The other six (001, 005, 007, 008, 009, 011) resolve boards holding Exquisite Blood, Throne of the God-Pharaoh, Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call or Mirkwood Bats, none of which is in the deck. Those proofs are still true about those cards and no longer about this deck.

The goldfish models a cast tutor as a wildcard that fills ONE missing any_of group, pays its mana and costs a turn when it puts the card on top. It does not model the two life, the lost draw, or the choice between two missing groups. This deck has exactly one tutor, so every *_assisted figure quoted here is Vampiric Tutor and nothing else, which makes the assisted-minus-unassisted gap a clean measure of this one card and still a ceiling on it.

Nothing measures fetch-versus-hold. No artifact prices the two life, the turn of delay, or the value of revealing nothing against a table's interaction, so every timing call here is coaching sitting on measured assembly rates.

Death-triggered drain is not modelled (goldfish meta: 'the largest known gap here'), the outlet-and-payoff pair is not measured (engine.json open_questions, settled_by goldfish), and Elenda, the Dusk Rose and Blade of the Bloodchief are dark to the model. Elenda is not a wish here for that reason: her token count under the doublers is engine.json's open question for resolve-stack, and no figure exists to rank her against the four fetches above.

strategic_frame.json and engine.json disagree on one word. The frame's role_assignment still calls stack 003 'the fastest verified kill in the 99'; engine.json's round-2 revision withdrew 'fastest' because no artifact measures kill speed for any route, and on availability the Bloodletter component assembles later (mean turn 6.707) than the Conqueror component (6.385). This guide follows engine.json. Reported, not edited.

No graveyard answer exists to fetch: deck-audit interaction-breadth reads graveyard 0 and land 0 among classes answered, and the card that carried graveyard exile (Immersturm Predator) left in v1.1.1. Against a reanimator seat this tutor buys speed and never an answer.

Purphoros, God of the Forge's oracle text is read from the corpus (cards.csv), not from this deck's artifacts. The stack scenario strategic_frame.json filed for it (which of the 99 removes Purphoros) is still open, and the '4 of 38' figure is Forge on v1.1.0, not on this sha. Despark's legality against it rests on Purphoros's printed mana value and rule 702.12b, not on a passing stack.

DECISION for the orchestrator, carried from strategic_frame.json: the pilot's direction says the lifegain infinite is out; the sleeved 99 holds two checker-passed two-card loops on Bloodthirsty Conqueror. The Conqueror wish is written and validated. If the direction means no two-card loop, that wish should be removed and the tutor's measured value on this deck falls to the Bloodletter gap (4.1% to 9.4%) plus the death-drain gap (37.2% to 48.2%).
